title: Higher-Degree Polynomial Replacements in Jarvis
summary: The low-degree case is associated with insecurity against Gröbner-basis attacks, while the effect of higher-degree replacements on algebraic properties and attack behavior remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For the Jarvis construction, whose affine layer is represented as $A=C\circ B^{-1}$, determine the algebraic structure and security consequences of replacing both polynomials $B$ and $C$ with polynomials of higher degree. The question is motivated by the existing low-degree case, where composing finite-field inversion with two low-degree affine polynomials produces algebraic properties associated with insecurity against Gr?bner-basis attacks; the unresolved task is to characterize how these properties and the resulting attack behavior change as the degrees of $B$ and $C$ increase.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of the Jarvis construction in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: The degrees of polynomials B and C, varied from the existing low-degree case to higher-degree choices
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the algebraic structure and security consequences, including the resulting attack behavior, when both B and C are replaced by higher-degree polynomials.

citations.label: Algebraic Cryptanalysis of STARK-Friendly Designs: Application to MARVELlous and MiMC

progress.summary: The source presents this as a natural question after demonstrating Gröbner-basis insecurity for Jarvis and Friday in the low-degree setting. It leaves the higher-degree replacement case open as a question about its algebraic and security consequences.
citation_labels: Martin R. Albrecht et al., Algebraic Cryptanalysis of STARK-Friendly Designs: Application to MARVELlous and MiMC
